title: One angry support ticket is not a problem. It's a signal.
description:
New PMs treat every loud request as a problem to solve, then wonder why they keep shipping fixes for symptoms. This Short breaks down the difference between a signal (one piece of raw evidence) and a problem (the validated pain a cluster of signals points to), using the B2B analytics worked example from Level 1's Problem Discovery lesson: two support tickets, a return-rate drop, and one lost renewal that all cluster into a single real problem. Collect signals, cluster them, then write the problem statement before anyone proposes a solution.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/product-manager-mastery-path/level-1/03-problem-discovery/

#Shorts

beats.narration: One angry support ticket is not a problem. It's a signal. So is a churn comment, a metric drop, a stakeholder request.
A signal is one piece of raw evidence. A problem is the validated pain a cluster of signals points to. Confuse them and you spend your sprint fixing symptoms.
So you collect signals for a week or two without committing to a fix. Then you cluster the ones pointing at the same underlying issue.

Two tickets about finding last month's report. A twelve percent drop in seven day return rate. One lost renewal. Three loose signals, one real problem: monthly users have no reason to come back between report cycles.
Validate the cluster, then write the problem statement before anyone proposes a solution. Fix the pattern, not the loudest ticket.
The full lesson has the worked example and the problem statement template.
